quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #6
										  					
  

50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: How does alcohol affect your reflexes and judgment?

options.text: Beer affects you less than wine.
Wine affects you less than beer.
Hard ciders and mixed drinks affect you the most.
It depends on how much alcohol is in your blood.

questions.correctAnswerText: It depends on how much alcohol is in your blood.
questions.explanation: Any type of alcohol harms your reflexes and judgment. The type of alcohol does not matter. Only the amount of alcohol in your blood matters.

questions.question: Your wheels drop off the pavement onto the shoulder. What should you do?

options.text: Brake hard and turn sharply back onto the pavement.
Stop your car on the edge of the road.
Slow down and carefully turn back onto the pavement.
Keep your speed and turn sharply back onto the pavement.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and carefully turn back onto the pavement.
questions.explanation: Reduce your speed without braking. Then carefully turn back onto the pavement. Watch for nearby traffic when you return to the road.

questions.question: When do roads become very slippery?

options.text: After it has been raining for an hour or more.
The day after it rains.
For the first 10 to 15 minutes of a rainstorm.
Right after the rain stops.

questions.correctAnswerText: For the first 10 to 15 minutes of a rainstorm.
questions.explanation: Roads become very slippery in the first 10 to 15 minutes of rain. The rain brings oil from the asphalt to the surface. Hot weather makes this worse because heat and water together push more oil to the surface.

questions.question: Before you start the car, you should:

options.text: Make sure only back seat passengers have buckled their seat belts.
Make sure only adult passengers have buckled their seat belts.
Make sure only child passengers have buckled their seat belts.
Make sure all passengers have buckled their seat belts.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure all passengers have buckled their seat belts.
questions.explanation: Develop a habit when getting in your car. Before you start the engine, buckle your seat belt and make sure all passengers do the same.

questions.question: Your power steering stops working while you drive. What should you do?

options.text: Honk your horn and turn off the engine.
Turn on your hazard lights and brace yourself.
Steer with effort, slow down, drive to a safe area, and stop.
Press hard on your brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Steer with effort, slow down, drive to a safe area, and stop.
questions.explanation: When power steering fails, steering becomes hard. Reduce your speed and pull off the road to a safe place to stop.

questions.question: What does a flashing yellow light mean?

options.text: Stop and look both ways, then go if it is safe.
Stop and wait for a green light.
Speed up to clear the intersection quickly.
Slow down and go carefully.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and go carefully.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means you should slow down and proceed with caution.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Intersection ahead.
Steep hill ahead.
Winding road ahead.
Merging traffic ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Steep hill ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a steep downhill grade is coming.

questions.question: When riding in a vehicle, small children:

options.text: Can be safely held by a strong adult.
Are safe if they stand on the floor in the back.
Will not be hurt in an accident because they are small.
Must never stand in the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must never stand in the vehicle.
questions.explanation: Children too small for regular seat belts need special child seats. No adult is strong enough to hold a child safe during an accident or sudden stop. Always keep children properly fastened in a seat.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No right turn.
You must turn right.
Watch for traffic on your right.
Don't park on the right side.

questions.correctAnswerText: No right turn.
questions.explanation: A red circle with a line through a symbol means that action is not allowed. In this case, the symbol shows a right turn, so right turns are not allowed.

questions.question: Lanes moving in the same direction are divided by ____ lines.

options.text: Yellow
White
Red
Black

questions.correctAnswerText: White
questions.explanation: Solid white lines separate lanes moving in the same direction and mark the right edge of the road. Broken white lines separate lanes moving the same way and can be crossed to pass. Yellow lines separate lanes moving in opposite directions.

questions.question: When can you park or stop on the shoulder of a freeway?

options.text: If you turn on your four-way emergency flashers.
If no part of your vehicle is on the road.
If you need to check a map for directions.
Only in an emergency.

questions.correctAnswerText: Only in an emergency.
questions.explanation: You cannot park on a freeway shoulder except during an emergency.

questions.question: Before turning left, you must:

options.text: Sound your horn.
Let oncoming vehicles pass first.
Move to the right side of your lane.
Wait for oncoming traffic to get a red light.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let oncoming vehicles pass first.
questions.explanation: When turning left, you must give the right-of-way to oncoming vehicles and pedestrians.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: The left lane is only for vehicles with a certain number of people inside.
You can only turn from certain lanes.
Do not enter.
Both lanes must merge smoothly together.

questions.correctAnswerText: The left lane is only for vehicles with a certain number of people inside.
questions.explanation: This is a high occupancy vehicle (HOV) lane sign. It is reserved for buses and vehicles with the driver plus one or more passengers, as shown on the sign.

questions.question: Which of these drugs can affect your driving?

options.text: Allergy medicine
Marijuana
Cold medicine
All of these

questions.correctAnswerText: All of these
questions.explanation: Many drugs can make it unsafe to drive. This includes illegal drugs, prescription medicines, and over-the-counter medicines. Driving while impaired by any drug is a crime.

questions.question: You are waiting in line at a stop sign. The cars ahead go through. If there is no traffic coming, what must you do?

options.text: You can go through without stopping again.
You must stop again at the stop sign before going.
You can roll slowly past the stop sign.
You can follow the car in front without stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must stop again at the stop sign before going.
questions.explanation: You must always come to a complete stop at a stop sign and check for traffic before going. Do not skip stopping just because other cars are moving.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: All traffic must turn right.
No right turns allowed.
All traffic must go straight.
A road is joining from the right.

questions.correctAnswerText: A road is joining from the right.
questions.explanation: This sign shows that a road is coming into this intersection from the right side.

questions.question: Can you drive around the gates at a railroad crossing?

options.text: Yes, after the train passes.
Never.
Yes, when the lights stop flashing.
Yes, if other drivers do it.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never.
questions.explanation: You must stop at railroad crossings when you see warning signals. These may include flashing red lights, lowered gates, a flagperson, or train sounds. Never go around a lowered gate.

questions.question: If a worker is directing traffic in a construction zone, you must:

options.text: Follow what the worker tells you to do.
Do what other cars are doing instead of listening to the worker.
Assume the worker should not be there.
Follow regular traffic laws and ignore the worker.

questions.correctAnswerText: Follow what the worker tells you to do.
questions.explanation: Always follow directions from a worker, sign, or police officer in a construction zone. Not doing so is illegal and dangerous to workers.

questions.question: When you see a steady yellow traffic light, what should you do?

options.text: Speed up to beat the red light.
Keep driving because you have the right-of-way.
Slow down and stop, unless you are already in the intersection.
Look at what the cars next to you are doing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and stop, unless you are already in the intersection.
questions.explanation: A yellow light means a red light is coming. Stop unless you have already entered the intersection.

questions.question: When should you look over your shoulder to check your blind spot?

options.text: When pulling toward or away from a curb.
When turning left or right.
When changing lanes.
In all of these situations.

questions.correctAnswerText: In all of these situations.
questions.explanation: Always check your blind spot by looking over your shoulder whenever you change your vehicle's position. This includes turning, changing lanes, or pulling toward or away from a curb.

questions.question: If you are in an accident, you should:

options.text: Stop your vehicle at or near the accident.
Not stand or walk in traffic lanes.
Turn off the engines of damaged vehicles.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: If you are in an accident, stop at or near the scene. Move your vehicle out of traffic if you can. Do not stand or walk in traffic lanes—another vehicle could hit you. Turn off the engines of damaged vehicles.

questions.question: If a crossing guard is directing traffic in a school zone, you must:

options.text: Follow the crossing guard's directions.
Follow what other cars are doing, even if the guard says otherwise.
Assume the guard should not be directing traffic.
Follow the normal rules as if no children were present.

questions.correctAnswerText: Follow the crossing guard's directions.
questions.explanation: Slow down and be careful when a sign, crossing guard, or police officer tells you to. Always drive carefully in a school zone.

questions.question: A fully loaded tractor-trailer traveling at 55 mph may take up to ____ to stop completely.

options.text: 50 feet
125 feet
400 feet
750 feet

questions.correctAnswerText: 400 feet
questions.explanation: Tractor-trailers need much longer distances to stop than small cars at the same speed. A fully loaded tractor-trailer may need almost 400 feet to stop when traveling at 55 mph.

questions.question: Always signal when:

options.text: Changing lanes.
Pulling into or out of a parking space.
Pulling into traffic from an alley or parking area.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Always use your turn signal when changing lanes, pulling into or out of a parking space, or pulling into traffic from an alley or parking area. Signal to warn other drivers and help prevent accidents.

questions.question: You should not pass another driver:

options.text: When there is a solid yellow line.
On a hill or curve in the road.
If oncoming traffic is near.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Do not pass when it could endanger you or other drivers. Never pass in no passing zones, where you cannot see ahead clearly, or when oncoming traffic is nearby.

questions.question: On slippery roads, you should:

options.text: Slow down.
Drive faster.
Drive at the speed limit with care.
Never drive faster than 20 mph.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: Slow down when you see rain, snow, or sleet. These create slippery roads. When conditions are bad, you may need to drive slower than the speed limit for safety.

questions.question: This sign shape and color means a ____ sign.

options.text: No passing zone
Wrong way
Railroad crossing
Stop

questions.correctAnswerText: No passing zone
questions.explanation: A pennant-shaped sign like this only marks a no passing zone.

questions.question: At a school crossing sign, you should:

options.text: Always stop, even if there is no stop sign.
Watch for children and be ready to stop.
Always honk your horn when you see children.
Help children cross the street.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch for children and be ready to stop.
questions.explanation: Yield to all pedestrians in a crosswalk. Watch carefully for pedestrians when you drive through intersections or turn corners.

questions.question: When entering a highway from an entrance ramp, you should:

options.text: Go faster than traffic to get ahead.
Go slowly to avoid other vehicles.
Stop first, then slowly enter traffic.
Speed up to match the traffic speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed up to match the traffic speed.
questions.explanation: Highway entrance ramps have acceleration lanes. When merging, turn on your signal, look for an opening, speed up to match traffic, and merge safely into traffic.

questions.question: If a driver is worried, nervous, angry, or crying, they:

options.text: Will drive the same as if they were calm.
Can drive faster because they are more alert.
Should calm down and focus before they start driving.
Should call a friend to talk while driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should calm down and focus before they start driving.
questions.explanation: You may not drive well if you are worried, excited, crying, angry, or sad. These emotions distract you because your mind is on something else. Calm down and focus before you start driving.

questions.question: How can you avoid making emergency stops while driving in traffic?

options.text: Honk your horn to warn other drivers.
Look ahead and keep a safe distance from other vehicles.
Drive only in the right lane.
Drive slower than the traffic around you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look ahead and keep a safe distance from other vehicles.
questions.explanation: A safe following distance gives you time to react to problems ahead. This prevents emergency stops that could cause drivers behind you to crash into your vehicle.

questions.question: When you borrow an unfamiliar vehicle from a friend, you should:

options.text: Not worry because all vehicles work the same way.
Hide from your friend that you don't know the vehicle.
Ignore any obvious problems to avoid embarrassing your friend.
Spend a few minutes learning how the vehicle's controls and equipment work.

questions.correctAnswerText: Spend a few minutes learning how the vehicle's controls and equipment work.
questions.explanation: Before driving an unfamiliar vehicle, learn where and how to use the turn signals, hazard lights, headlights, windshield wipers, brakes, gear selector, and horn. Fix any problems before you drive.

questions.question: What is the first thing you should adjust when you get into a car?

options.text: Your seat belt
The steering wheel
Your rearview mirror
Your seat

questions.correctAnswerText: Your seat
questions.explanation: First adjust your seat so you are comfortable and can see the road clearly. Then adjust your mirrors and steering wheel based on your seat position.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: The road is getting wider.
The right lane is ending soon.
A highway entrance ramp is coming.
The left lane is ending soon.

questions.correctAnswerText: The right lane is ending soon.
questions.explanation: This sign tells you that the right lane will end ahead.

questions.question: When you see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights, you must:

options.text: Slow down and stay in your lane.
Keep driving in your lane.
Pull to the right side and stop.
Stop right where you are.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the right side and stop.
questions.explanation: When you see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights or hear a siren, pull to the right side of the road and stop immediately.

questions.question: A reflective orange triangle on the back of a vehicle means:

options.text: It is a slow-moving vehicle.
It is an ambulance.
It is a school bus.
The vehicle is broken down.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is a slow-moving vehicle.
questions.explanation: An orange triangle on the back of a vehicle means it travels slower than 25 mph. You may see this on farm equipment, construction vehicles, and horse-drawn wagons.

questions.question: Which of the following helps direct drivers into the correct lanes for turning on highways?

options.text: Flashing red lights
Flashing yellow lights
White lines on the side of the road
White arrows painted on the road

questions.correctAnswerText: White arrows painted on the road
questions.explanation: Arrows on the road show which lanes to use for different purposes, such as going straight or turning.

questions.question: When entering a roadway from a private road or driveway, you should:

options.text: Honk your horn to warn drivers.
Partly block the roadway to alert other drivers.
Drive out quickly to merge with traffic.
Let pedestrians and roadway traffic go first.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let pedestrians and roadway traffic go first.
questions.explanation: When entering a roadway from a driveway or private road, you must let pedestrians and traffic on the roadway go first.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Keep right.
Low shoulder ahead.
No parking at any time.
The lane is ending.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep right.
questions.explanation: This sign tells drivers to stay in the right lane to avoid a hazard ahead.

questions.question: At a railroad crossing with more than one track, you should:

options.text: Wait until you can see clearly down all tracks before moving.
Stop on the first track and watch for another train.
Go as soon as the train passes.
Go when one track is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until you can see clearly down all tracks before moving.
questions.explanation: At a railroad crossing with more than one track, do not move as soon as a train passes. Make sure you can see clearly down all tracks before crossing. Even at single-track crossings, always check again for another approaching train.

questions.question: A steady yellow traffic signal means a ____ light will appear soon.

options.text: Flashing yellow
Steady green
Steady red
Flashing red

questions.correctAnswerText: Steady red
questions.explanation: A steady yellow light means a steady red light is coming next.

questions.question: You may cross solid yellow lines:

options.text: To pass traffic moving in the same direction.
During daylight hours only.
At any time.
When making turns.

questions.correctAnswerText: When making turns.
questions.explanation: Broken lines can be crossed, but solid lines cannot. You can only cross a solid yellow line when you are turning.

questions.question: Compared to driving during the day, driving at night is:

options.text: Less dangerous.
No more or less dangerous.
More dangerous.
Easier on your eyes.

questions.correctAnswerText: More dangerous.
questions.explanation: Night driving is more dangerous. You cannot see as well in the dark. Headlights from other cars can blind you. More tired and impaired drivers are on the road at night.

questions.question: An inattentive driver is one who:

options.text: Looks away from the road or daydreams while driving.
Makes eye contact with a passenger while driving.
Only watches the car ahead.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Do not look at passengers, search for things in your car, read, sightsee, or daydream while driving. Always scan the road, check your mirrors, and watch your instruments. These habits keep you a safe, attentive driver.

questions.question: When you drive through an area where children are playing, expect them to:

options.text: Know when it is safe to cross the street.
Stop at the curb before crossing the street.
Run out in front of you without looking.
Not cross the street unless they are with an adult.

questions.correctAnswerText: Run out in front of you without looking.
questions.explanation: Slow down and be extra careful when children are nearby. They may not understand danger and could run in front of you without looking.

questions.question: When you meet a car with blinding headlights, you should:

options.text: Use your bright lights until the other car dims theirs.
Flash your lights on and off to warn the other driver.
Dim your lights and then speed up to pass quickly.
Look toward the right side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look toward the right side of the road.
questions.explanation: If an oncoming car has high beams on, look away from the headlights and toward the right side of the road until it passes. This prevents you from being blinded.

questions.question: If your car starts to skid, turn your steering wheel:

options.text: To keep the front wheels straight.
In the direction you want the vehicle to go.
In the opposite direction of the skid.
In any direction. It does not matter.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the direction you want the vehicle to go.
questions.explanation: In a skid, turn your steering wheel in the direction you want to go. When the vehicle straightens out, turn the wheel the other way.

questions.question: Before passing another vehicle, you should signal:

options.text: Just before changing lanes.
At any time.
After changing lanes.
Early enough for others to know your plans.

questions.correctAnswerText: Early enough for others to know your plans.
questions.explanation: Signal early enough before passing so other drivers know what you plan to do ahead of time.

questions.question: Crossbuck signs indicate:

options.text: Railroad crossings.
School zones.
No passing zones.
Hospitals.

questions.correctAnswerText: Railroad crossings.
questions.explanation: Crossbuck signs tell drivers to yield to trains at a railroad crossing. Never try to outrun a train.

questions.question: While driving, your wheels slip off the edge of the road. You should:

options.text: Jerk the steering wheel to force the vehicle back onto the pavement.
Speed up and steer back onto the pavement gradually.
Slam on your brakes and stop.
Slow down gently using the brakes. Turn the steering wheel to return to the pavement at a safe speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down gently using the brakes. Turn the steering wheel to return to the pavement at a safe speed.
questions.explanation: If your wheels leave the road, keep driving off the pavement. Gently brake to slow down. When safe, turn the wheel to get back on the pavement. Do not sharply jerk the wheel to force your vehicle back on the road.
